c1-gen-0062: The word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision. Read Genesis 15:1.
c2-gen-0021: God set out food for people and for every beast and bird. Read Genesis 1:29 and Genesis 1:30.
c2-gen-0022: On the way up the mountain, Isaac asked where the lamb was. Read Genesis 22:8 and Genesis 22:14.
c2-gen-0023: God put His bow in the cloud. See what He does in Genesis 9:15 and Genesis 9:16.
c3-gen-0003: Jacob blessed Judah, and his brothers would bow down to him. Read Genesis 49:8 and Genesis 49:10.
c3-gen-0004: Abram looked up and tried to count the stars. Let's read Genesis 15:5 and Genesis 22:17.
c3-gen-0005: God promised a blessing for all the families of the earth. Read Genesis 12:3 and Genesis 22:18.
c3-gen-0006: God spoke of enemies and a big promise for Abraham's family. Read Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 22:17.
c1-gen-0063: Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen were quarreling. Hear Abram in Genesis 13:8.
c2-gen-0024: Abram would not take even a thread from the king of Sodom. Read Genesis 14:22 and Genesis 14:23.
c2-gen-0025: A priest-king brought out bread and wine and blessed Abram. Read Genesis 14:18 and Genesis 14:20.
c2-gen-0026: Jacob felt tricked and asked Laban why. Hear Laban in Genesis 29:25 and Genesis 29:26.
c3-gen-0007: Jacob's family put away their false gods and set out for Bethel. Read Genesis 35:2, Genesis 35:4, and Genesis 35:5.
c3-gen-0008: God told Jacob that nations and kings would come from him. Look back with Genesis 17:16 and Genesis 35:11.
c3-gen-0009: Three women waited and hoped for a baby. Let's read Genesis 11:30, Genesis 25:21, and Genesis 30:22.
c3-gen-0010: Two brothers had a hard past, and then their father Isaac died. Read Genesis 25:33, Genesis 25:34, and Genesis 35:29.
c1-exo-0022: At Sinai, God reminded Israel of all He had done. Read Exodus 19:4.
c2-exo-0019: Thunder rolled, and Moses told the trembling people not to fear. Read Exodus 20:20.
c2-exo-0020: The people stood far off, shaking with fear. Watch Moses in Exodus 20:19 and Exodus 20:21.
c2-exo-0021: Your enemy's ox wandered off. What now? Read Exodus 23:4 and Exodus 23:5.
c3-exo-0003: God had a plan for clearing the land, and it was not all in one year. Read Exodus 23:29 and Exodus 23:30.
c3-exo-0004: God told His people to be kind to strangers. Let's read Exodus 22:21 and Exodus 23:9.
c3-exo-0005: Twice at Sinai, the people made a promise to God. Read Exodus 19:8 and Exodus 24:7.
c3-exo-0006: God made promises to the people who obey His voice. Read Exodus 19:5 and Exodus 23:22.
c1-lev-0003: The fiftieth year was a special time in Israel. Read Leviticus 25:10.
c2-lev-0007: The people wondered what they would eat in the seventh year. God had an answer in Leviticus 25:20 and Leviticus 25:21.
c2-lev-0008: God made a rule about selling the land. Find out why in Leviticus 25:23 and Leviticus 25:24.
c2-lev-0009: God wants honest scales and fair weights. Read Leviticus 19:35 and Leviticus 19:36.
c3-lev-0001: Every Sabbath, the bread was set in order before the LORD. Read Leviticus 24:8 and Leviticus 24:9.
c3-lev-0002: God tells His people to fear Him. Then He speaks of a brother who has become poor. Read Leviticus 19:32 and Leviticus 25:36.
c3-lev-0003: God gave the land its own rest every seventh year. Read Leviticus 25:4, Leviticus 26:34, and Leviticus 26:35.
c3-lev-0004: God cares about the person living among His people, and about the poor. Read Leviticus 19:34 and Leviticus 25:35.
c1-num-0003: On Mount Hor, Moses took off Aaron's priestly clothes. Read Numbers 20:26 and Numbers 20:28.
c2-num-0008: Joshua asked Moses to stop the men. Hear Moses answer in Numbers 11:28 and Numbers 11:29.
c2-num-0009: Miriam and Aaron spoke up against Moses. Read Numbers 12:2 and Numbers 12:3.
c2-num-0010: A plague began, and Aaron ran in with incense. Read Numbers 16:47 and Numbers 16:48.
c3-num-0001: Korah's group said hard words to Moses and Aaron. Read Numbers 16:3 and Numbers 16:7.
c3-num-0002: God said the rod of the man He chose would blossom. Let's read Numbers 16:5, Numbers 17:5, and Numbers 17:8.
c3-num-0003: God shared the Spirit with the seventy elders. Then came Joshua's turn. Read Numbers 11:17 and Numbers 27:20.
c3-num-0004: Moses and Aaron called on God by a special name. Read Numbers 16:22 and Numbers 27:16.
c1-deu-0005: Moses died in the land of Moab. Read Deuteronomy 34:6.
c2-deu-0013: Judges must be fair and not afraid of anyone. Hear Moses in Deuteronomy 1:17.
c2-deu-0014: Moses begged to cross over and see the good land. Read Deuteronomy 3:25 and Deuteronomy 3:26.
c2-deu-0015: Israel was the least of all peoples, yet God chose them. Read Deuteronomy 7:7 and Deuteronomy 7:8.
c3-deu-0001: In Egypt, crops were watered by foot. The new land was different. Read Deuteronomy 11:10 and Deuteronomy 11:11.
c3-deu-0002: A future king was to copy God's law for himself. Let's read Deuteronomy 17:18, Deuteronomy 17:20, and Deuteronomy 31:9.
c3-deu-0003: Moses went up Pisgah and looked out at the land. Read Deuteronomy 3:27 and Deuteronomy 34:4.
c3-deu-0004: God wants His words taught to children. Read Deuteronomy 11:19 and Deuteronomy 31:13.
c1-1ch-0001: Saul did not keep the word of the LORD. Let's read First Chronicles 10:13 and First Chronicles 10:14.
c2-1ch-0001: David lived in a cedar house, but the ark was under tent curtains. Read First Chronicles 17:1 and First Chronicles 17:2.
c2-1ch-0002: David would not build God's house, but a son was coming. Read First Chronicles 22:8 and First Chronicles 22:9.
c2-1ch-0003: Gad gave David three hard choices. Hear David in First Chronicles 21:12 and First Chronicles 21:13.
c3-1ch-0001: David called on the LORD, and heaven answered at the altar. Read First Chronicles 21:26 and First Chronicles 21:27.
c3-1ch-0002: David worked hard to gather gold, silver, bronze, and iron. Then he prayed. Read First Chronicles 22:14 and First Chronicles 29:14.
c3-1ch-0003: God told David he would not build Him a house. Hear David explain in First Chronicles 17:4 and First Chronicles 28:3.
c3-1ch-0004: The LORD searches every heart. Listen to David's prayer in First Chronicles 28:9 and First Chronicles 29:17.
c1-1ch-0002: David said the first to attack the Jebusites would be chief. Read First Chronicles 11:6.
c2-1ch-0004: Three mighty men broke through the camp to bring David water. Read First Chronicles 11:18 and First Chronicles 11:19.
c2-1ch-0005: Day by day, more men came to help David. Read First Chronicles 12:22 and First Chronicles 12:32.
c2-1ch-0006: David was afraid to bring the ark into his city. Read First Chronicles 13:13 and First Chronicles 13:14.
c3-1ch-0005: Two brothers made a deal to help each other in battle. Read First Chronicles 19:12 and First Chronicles 19:13.
c3-1ch-0006: The first try to bring back the ark went wrong. Read First Chronicles 13:3 and First Chronicles 15:13.
c3-1ch-0007: The first time, the ark rode on a new cart. Read First Chronicles 13:7 and First Chronicles 15:15.
c3-1ch-0008: The LORD was with David. Let's read First Chronicles 11:9 and First Chronicles 18:6.
c1-2ch-0001: A great crowd came against Judah, and Jahaziel stood up. Read Second Chronicles 20:15.
c2-2ch-0002: Solomon stood, then knelt, where all Israel could see him pray. Look at Second Chronicles 6:12 and Second Chronicles 6:13.
c2-2ch-0003: King Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he set himself to seek the LORD. Pray along with Second Chronicles 20:3 and Second Chronicles 20:12.
c2-2ch-0004: Judah marched out into the Wilderness of Tekoa. Listen to the king in Second Chronicles 20:20 and Second Chronicles 20:21.
c3-2ch-0001: A huge army came, and King Asa cried out to the LORD. Read Second Chronicles 14:6 and Second Chronicles 14:11.
c3-2ch-0002: God gave a serious warning about His house. Let's open Second Chronicles 7:20 and Second Chronicles 36:19.
c3-2ch-0003: King Manasseh was in trouble, so he humbled himself and prayed. Read Second Chronicles 7:14, Second Chronicles 33:12, and Second Chronicles 33:13.
c3-2ch-0004: Solomon asked God to hear from heaven. Later, Hezekiah prayed for the worshipers. Read Second Chronicles 6:21 and Second Chronicles 30:20.
c1-2ch-0002: Josiah was still young in the eighth year of his reign. Read Second Chronicles 34:3.
c2-2ki-0016: Workmen were fixing up the temple, and Josiah sent the money. Read Second Kings 22:7.
c2-2ch-0005: A book was found, and Josiah sent men to ask the LORD. Read Second Chronicles 34:21 and Second Chronicles 34:22.
c2-2ki-0017: King Josiah read God's book out loud to all the people. Read Second Kings 23:2 and Second Kings 23:3.
c3-2ch-0005: Passover was coming, and Josiah spoke to the Levites about the holy ark. Read Second Chronicles 35:2 and Second Chronicles 35:3.
c3-2ki-0001: Josiah did not turn aside to the right or the left. Read Second Kings 22:2 and Second Kings 23:25.
c3-2ki-0002: Josiah was afraid of the LORD's anger, even after all his changes. Read Second Kings 22:13 and Second Kings 23:26.
c3-2ch-0006: Josiah made a promise to keep God's commands, and then he held a Passover. Read Second Chronicles 34:31 and Second Chronicles 35:18.
c1-ecc-0001: The Preacher says two are better than one. He says more in Ecclesiastes 4:12.
c2-ecc-0001: All the rivers run into the sea, the Preacher says. Read Ecclesiastes 1:7.
c2-ecc-0002: The Preacher says there is a season for everything. See God's work in Ecclesiastes 3:1 and Ecclesiastes 3:11.
c2-ecc-0003: Do not be rash with your mouth, the Preacher warns. Read Ecclesiastes 5:2 and Ecclesiastes 5:3.
c3-ecc-0001: The Preacher saw that the race is not to the swift. Let's read Ecclesiastes 9:11 and Ecclesiastes 9:12.
c3-ecc-0002: Enjoying good things from your work comes from God's hand. Read Ecclesiastes 2:24 and Ecclesiastes 3:13.
c3-ecc-0003: The Preacher tells the young man to rejoice in his youth. Then read on in Ecclesiastes 11:9 and Ecclesiastes 12:1.
c3-ecc-0004: The book starts with Vanity of vanities, and it ends with a big wrap-up. Read Ecclesiastes 1:2 and Ecclesiastes 12:13.
c1-sng-0001: The bride calls herself the lily of the valleys. Read Song of Solomon 2:1.
c2-sng-0001: Something is spoiling the vines with tender grapes. Find it in Song of Solomon 2:15.
c2-sng-0002: The beloved calls his love to rise up and come away. Hear why in Song of Solomon 2:10 and Song of Solomon 2:11.
c2-sng-0003: My beloved is mine, and I am his, she says. Read Song of Solomon 2:16 and Song of Solomon 2:17.
c3-sng-0001: The bride tells the daughters of Jerusalem not to stir up love. Read Song of Solomon 2:7 and Song of Solomon 5:8.
c3-sng-0002: Solomon's vineyard brought in lots of silver, but love is different. Read Song of Solomon 8:7 and Song of Solomon 8:11.
c3-sng-0003: The beloved says her love is better than wine. Then read on in Song of Solomon 4:10 and Song of Solomon 8:6.
c3-sng-0004: Her beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Let's read Song of Solomon 2:9 and Song of Solomon 8:14.
c1-lam-0001: Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed. Read Lamentations 3:22 and Lamentations 3:23.
c2-lam-0001: The city was once full of people and great among the nations. Read Lamentations 1:1.
c2-lam-0002: Therefore I hope in Him! the writer says. Let's read Lamentations 3:24 and Lamentations 3:25.
c2-lam-0003: Let us lift our hearts and hands to God in heaven. Read Lamentations 3:40 and Lamentations 3:41.
c3-lam-0001: The writer says the Lord will not cast off forever, and He will show compassion. Read Lamentations 3:31, Lamentations 3:32, and Lamentations 3:33.
c3-lam-0002: Jerusalem wept, but God drew near when the writer called. Read Lamentations 1:16 and Lamentations 3:57.
c3-lam-0003: Even with Mount Zion empty, the writer looked to the LORD's throne. Read Lamentations 3:22 and Lamentations 5:19.
c3-lam-0004: The sons of Zion were worth more than fine gold. Read Lamentations 2:15 and Lamentations 4:2.
c1-hos-0001: God spoke to Hosea and told him to take a wife. Read Hosea 1:3.
c2-hos-0001: God loved Israel when Israel was a child. Read Hosea 11:1.
c2-hos-0002: God speaks comfort to her in the wilderness and gives her vineyards. Read Hosea 2:14 and Hosea 2:15.
c2-hos-0003: In that day, she will call Him My Husband. Read Hosea 2:16 and Hosea 2:17.
c3-hos-0001: God taught Ephraim to walk, holding them by their arms. Read Hosea 11:3 and Hosea 11:4.
c3-hos-0002: To those who were not His people, God says, You are My people! Read Hosea 1:9 and Hosea 2:23.
c3-hos-0003: How can I give you up, Ephraim? God cries. Read Hosea 11:8 and Hosea 14:8.
c3-hos-0004: O Israel, return to the LORD your God. Read Hosea 3:5 and Hosea 14:1.
c1-hos-0002: Ephraim mixed himself in with the other peoples. Read Hosea 7:8.
c2-hos-0004: O Ephraim, what shall I do to you? the LORD asks. Read Hosea 6:4.
c2-hos-0005: They sow the wind, Hosea says. Read Hosea 8:7 and Hosea 10:13.
c2-hos-0006: Israel called to Egypt and went to Assyria instead of the LORD. Read Hosea 7:10 and Hosea 7:11.
c3-hos-0005: Hosea says to sow righteousness and reap in mercy, for it is time to seek the LORD. Read Hosea 10:12 and Hosea 12:6.
c3-hos-0006: The people say they will return to the LORD, for He will heal them. Read Hosea 5:15 and Hosea 6:1.
c3-hos-0007: God wants mercy, not sacrifice. Let's read Hosea 6:6 and Hosea 13:4.
c3-hos-0008: God found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. Read Hosea 9:10 and Hosea 13:5.
c1-jol-0001: Locusts ruined the land, and Joel called the people back. Read Joel 2:13.
c2-jol-0001: The LORD's vine was laid waste, and His fig tree stripped bare. Read Joel 1:7.
c2-jol-0002: I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh, says the LORD. Let's read Joel 2:28 and Joel 2:29.
c2-jol-0003: Locusts everywhere, and Joel told the priests to set apart a fast. Read Joel 1:14 and Joel 1:15.
c3-jol-0001: The LORD will roar from Zion, and heaven and earth will shake. Read Joel 3:16 and Joel 3:17.
c3-jol-0002: Joel calls for the trumpet to sound in Zion, for the day of the LORD is coming. Read Joel 2:1 and Joel 3:14.
c3-jol-0003: Four kinds of locusts ate and ate. But God made a promise. Read Joel 1:4 and Joel 2:25.
c3-jol-0004: The sun goes dark and the moon turns red. Look up in Joel 2:31 and Joel 3:15.
c1-amo-0001: Before he spoke for the LORD, Amos had another life. Read Amos 1:1.
c2-amo-0001: They sold good people for silver. God saw it all. Read Amos 2:6.
c2-amo-0002: Can two walk together? Amos asks a string of questions. Read Amos 3:3 and Amos 3:4.
c2-amo-0003: The LORD spoke of the winter house and the summer house. Read Amos 3:14 and Amos 3:15.
c3-amo-0001: No bread, no rain. God kept calling His people. Read Amos 4:6 and Amos 4:8.
c3-amo-0002: Of all the families of the earth, God knew Israel. Read Amos 3:2 and Amos 4:12.
c3-amo-0003: A lion has roared! Who will not fear? Read Amos 1:2 and Amos 3:8.
c3-amo-0004: Some people on the mountain of Samaria were hurting the poor. Read Amos 3:9 and Amos 4:1.
c1-amo-0002: Amos, what do you see? the Lord asked in a vision. Read Amos 7:7 and Amos 7:8.
c2-amo-0004: Let justice run down like water, says the LORD. Read Amos 5:23 and Amos 5:24.
c2-amo-0005: God told Israel not to seek Bethel or enter Gilgal. Read Amos 5:4 and Amos 5:5.
c2-amo-0006: Amaziah the priest told Amos to go away to Judah. Read Amos 7:12 and Amos 7:13.
c3-amo-0005: Beds of ivory, bowls of wine, the best oils. But something was missing. Read Amos 6:4 and Amos 6:6.
c3-amo-0006: Amos saw locusts in a vision and begged the Lord to forgive. Read Amos 7:2 and Amos 9:8.
c3-amo-0007: The day of the LORD will be darkness, and not light. Read Amos 5:18 and Amos 8:9.
c3-amo-0008: The virgin of Israel has fallen, with no one to raise her up. Read Amos 5:2 and Amos 9:11.
c1-mic-0001: God's word came to Micah when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings. Read Micah 1:1.
c2-mic-0002: Micah tells of a day when nations turn swords into farm tools. Read Micah 4:3.
c2-mic-0003: Everyone will sit under his own vine and fig tree. Read Micah 4:4 and Micah 4:5.
c2-mic-0004: Leaders took bribes, and priests taught for pay. Read Micah 3:11 and Micah 3:12.
c3-mic-0001: Micah spoke of a Ruler coming to Israel. Let's read Micah 5:2 and Micah 5:3.
c3-mic-0002: The faithful man was gone, and people were planning evil. Read Micah 2:1 and Micah 7:2.
c3-mic-0003: Many nations say, He will teach us His ways. Read Micah 3:12 and Micah 4:2.
c3-mic-0004: The coming One will feed His flock in the strength of the LORD. Read Micah 5:4 and Micah 7:3.
c1-mic-0002: He has shown you, O man, what is good. Let's read Micah 6:8.
c2-mic-0005: The LORD will have compassion on us again. Read Micah 7:19.
c2-mic-0006: Who is a God like You? Micah asks. Read Micah 7:17 and Micah 7:18.
c2-mic-0007: O My people, what have I done to you? Hear the LORD in Micah 6:3 and Micah 6:4.
c3-mic-0005: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy! Read Micah 7:7 and Micah 7:8.
c3-mic-0006: God will save His people, just like when they left Egypt. Read Micah 4:10 and Micah 7:15.
c3-mic-0007: Micah ends his book with a promise God swore long ago. Read Micah 6:2 and Micah 7:20.
c3-mic-0008: Like dew from the LORD, the remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples. Read Micah 4:7 and Micah 5:7.
c1-hab-0001: Habakkuk cried out because it seemed God was not listening. Read Habakkuk 1:1 and Habakkuk 1:2.
c2-hab-0001: Write the vision, God told Habakkuk. Read Habakkuk 2:2.
c2-hab-0002: The proud man's soul is not upright. Read Habakkuk 2:3 and Habakkuk 2:4.
c2-hab-0003: One day the whole earth will know the glory of the LORD. Read Habakkuk 2:13 and Habakkuk 2:14.
c3-hab-0001: Idols have no breath at all. But the LORD is in His holy temple. Read Habakkuk 2:19 and Habakkuk 2:20.
c3-hab-0002: Habakkuk asked God to revive His work. Let's pray along with Habakkuk 1:12 and Habakkuk 3:2.
c3-hab-0003: The fig tree may not blossom, and the fields may be bare. Read Habakkuk 1:3, Habakkuk 3:17, and Habakkuk 3:18.
c3-hab-0004: The LORD God is my strength, Habakkuk says. Read Habakkuk 2:1 and Habakkuk 3:19.
c1-hag-0001: Go up to the mountains, God told the people. Read Haggai 1:8.
c2-hag-0001: The people said it was not time yet to build God's house. Read Haggai 1:4.
c2-hag-0002: Haggai told the people to consider their ways. They worked hard but never had enough. Read Haggai 1:5 and Haggai 1:6.
c2-hag-0003: Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people obeyed the LORD. Read Haggai 1:12 and Haggai 1:13.
c3-hag-0001: The new temple looked like nothing in their eyes. But God had a promise. Read Haggai 2:3 and Haggai 2:9.
c3-hag-0002: The people said, The time has not come. Then the work began again. Read Haggai 1:2 and Haggai 2:19.
c3-hag-0003: The LORD called for a drought on the land. Read Haggai 1:11 and Haggai 2:17.
c3-hag-0004: The LORD stirred up Zerubbabel's spirit. Read Haggai 1:14 and Haggai 2:23.
c1-zec-0001: Return to Me, says the LORD of hosts. Hear the rest in Zechariah 1:2 and Zechariah 1:3.
c2-zec-0001: At night, Zechariah saw a man riding a red horse. Read Zechariah 1:8.
c2-zec-0002: Up, Zion! Escape! The LORD warns the nations who hurt His people. Read Zechariah 2:7 and Zechariah 2:8.
c2-zec-0003: Joshua the high priest stood there in filthy clothes. Watch God's kindness in Zechariah 3:3 and Zechariah 3:4.
c3-zec-0001: Not by might nor by power. Let's read Zechariah 4:6 and Zechariah 4:7.
c3-zec-0002: Let your hands be strong! The temple was being built. Read Zechariah 4:10 and Zechariah 8:9.
c3-zec-0003: God loves Jerusalem with great zeal, and He is coming back. Read Zechariah 1:14 and Zechariah 8:3.
c3-zec-0004: Many nations will be joined to the LORD. Picture it in Zechariah 2:11 and Zechariah 8:23.
c1-zec-0002: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion! Zechariah says her King is coming. Read Zechariah 9:9.
c2-zec-0004: God promised to free His people from the waterless pit. Read Zechariah 9:11 and Zechariah 9:12.
c2-zec-0005: Zechariah took two staffs and named one Beauty. Read Zechariah 11:7 and Zechariah 11:10.
c2-zec-0006: All the nations gathered against Jerusalem. Let's read Zechariah 12:2 and Zechariah 12:3.
c3-zec-0005: After great mourning in Jerusalem, God provided for sin and uncleanness. Read Zechariah 12:11 and Zechariah 13:1.
c3-zec-0006: One day the LORD shall be King over all the earth. Read Zechariah 13:9 and Zechariah 14:9.
c3-zec-0007: The coming King will speak peace to the nations. Read Zechariah 9:10 and Zechariah 12:10.
c3-zec-0008: God will cut off the names of the idols from the land. Read Zechariah 13:2 and Zechariah 14:20.
c1-jos-0016: Before the battle in the north, the LORD spoke to Joshua. Read Joshua 11:6.
c2-jos-0008: God told Joshua to set up special cities for someone who hurt a person by accident. Read Joshua 20:2 and Joshua 20:3.
c2-jos-0009: Caleb remembered the day Moses sent him to spy out the land. Read Joshua 14:6 and Joshua 14:7.
c2-jos-0010: Reuben and Gad built a big altar by the border, and it got a name. Read Joshua 22:33 and Joshua 22:34.
c3-jos-0003: Joshua sent the tribes home with a charge to love the LORD. Read Joshua 22:4 and Joshua 22:5.
c3-jos-0004: God kept every promise He made to their fathers. Read Joshua 13:1 and Joshua 21:43.
c3-jos-0005: Caleb asked for the mountain where the Anakim lived. Read Joshua 11:22 and Joshua 14:12.
c3-jos-0006: Someone running to a city of refuge had to tell his story to the elders. Read Joshua 20:4 and Joshua 22:30.
c1-2sa-0015: Absalom got up early and stood beside the road to the gate. Read Second Samuel 15:2 and Second Samuel 15:4.
c2-2sa-0003: David learned that Ahithophel had joined Absalom, so he prayed. Read Second Samuel 15:31.
c2-2sa-0004: David told Ittai, a man from another land, to go back. Hear Ittai in Second Samuel 15:19 and Second Samuel 15:21.
c2-2sa-0005: Shimei cursed David, and Abishai wanted to stop him. Hear David in Second Samuel 16:10 and Second Samuel 16:11.
c3-2sa-0001: Hushai said David and his men were very angry. Hear his picture in Second Samuel 17:7 and Second Samuel 17:8.
c3-2sa-0002: David ran from Jerusalem, and friends brought honey, sheep, and cheese. Read Second Samuel 15:14 and Second Samuel 17:29.
c3-2sa-0003: Hushai came to meet David at the top of the mountain. Read Second Samuel 15:32 and Second Samuel 17:15.
c3-2sa-0004: A runner was coming, and the watchman was looking. Read Second Samuel 16:12 and Second Samuel 18:27.
c1-2sa-0016: At Gath lived a very tall man born to the giant. Read Second Samuel 21:20.
c2-2sa-0006: Abishai came to help David, and then David's men made a promise. Read Second Samuel 21:16 and Second Samuel 21:17.
c2-2sa-0007: Eleazar stood firm and fought until his hand was tired. Read Second Samuel 23:9 and Second Samuel 23:10.
c2-2sa-0008: The people ran, but Shammah stood in the middle of a field. Read Second Samuel 23:11 and Second Samuel 23:12.
c3-2sa-0005: Benaiah went down into a pit and faced a lion. Read Second Samuel 23:20 and Second Samuel 23:22.
c3-2sa-0006: David saw the angel striking the people, and he spoke up. Read Second Samuel 24:15 and Second Samuel 24:17.
c3-2sa-0007: David would not drink water won at great risk. Later, Araunah made him an offer. Read Second Samuel 23:17 and Second Samuel 24:24.
c3-2sa-0008: The angel stretched out his hand over Jerusalem, and the LORD relented. Read Second Samuel 21:15 and Second Samuel 24:16.
c1-1ki-0018: The priests brought in the ark and came out of the holy place. Read First Kings 8:10 and First Kings 8:11.
c2-1ki-0012: On the eighth day, Solomon sent the people home. Read First Kings 8:66.
c2-1ki-0013: Solomon said even heaven cannot contain God. Hear his prayer in First Kings 8:27 and First Kings 8:28.
c2-1ki-0014: Solomon asked God to hear, forgive, and act. Read First Kings 8:38 and First Kings 8:39.
c3-1ki-0001: Solomon loved many women from nations God had warned about. Read First Kings 11:2 and First Kings 11:4.
c3-1ki-0002: God warned Solomon about turning away, but He kept part of the kingdom. Read First Kings 9:6 and First Kings 11:13.
c3-1ki-0003: Solomon prayed that all the earth would know the LORD is God. Read First Kings 8:60 and First Kings 11:9.
c3-1ki-0004: Solomon called the temple an exalted house. Read First Kings 8:13 and First Kings 9:8.
c1-2ki-0006: A watchman saw riders coming toward Jezreel. Read Second Kings 9:20.
c2-2ki-0018: A young prophet took a flask of oil to anoint Jehu. Read Second Kings 9:1 and Second Kings 9:3.
c2-2ki-0019: Jehu came out to his officers, and one asked, Is all well? Read Second Kings 9:11 and Second Kings 9:12.

c2-1th-0001: Paul and his friends were gentle with the Thessalonians. Read First Thessalonians 2:7.
c2-1th-0002: Paul missed his friends and wanted so much to see them. Read First Thessalonians 2:17 and First Thessalonians 2:18.
c2-1th-0003: Paul prayed night and day for his friends in Thessalonica. Read First Thessalonians 3:9 and First Thessalonians 3:10.
c3-1th-0001: God will bring with Him those who sleep in Jesus. Read First Thessalonians 4:13 and First Thessalonians 4:14.
c3-1th-0002: Paul prayed for them to have more and more love. Read First Thessalonians 3:12 and First Thessalonians 4:9.
c3-1th-0003: Jesus saves us from the wrath to come. Read First Thessalonians 1:10 and First Thessalonians 5:9.
c3-1th-0004: Paul urges them to walk worthy of God, who calls them. Read First Thessalonians 2:12 and First Thessalonians 4:12.
c1-2th-0001: Paul reminds them of a rule about work. Read Second Thessalonians 3:10.
c2-2th-0001: Paul wrote a goodbye with his own hand. Read Second Thessalonians 3:17.
c2-2th-0002: Paul asks them not to be shaken in mind or troubled by a letter. Read Second Thessalonians 2:1 and Second Thessalonians 2:2.
c2-2th-0003: What do you do when someone will not obey? Read Second Thessalonians 3:14 and Second Thessalonians 3:15.
c3-2th-0001: Paul wanted to be an example for them to follow. Read Second Thessalonians 3:8 and Second Thessalonians 3:9.
c3-2th-0002: Paul prays that the Lord of peace will give them peace always. Read Second Thessalonians 2:16 and Second Thessalonians 3:16.
c3-2th-0003: God calls His people into His kingdom. Read Second Thessalonians 1:5 and Second Thessalonians 2:14.
c3-2th-0004: Paul prays for his friends, and he asks them to pray for him too. Read Second Thessalonians 1:11 and Second Thessalonians 3:1.
c1-1ti-0001: Paul gives a faithful saying, worthy of all acceptance. Read First Timothy 1:15.
c2-1ti-0001: Paul tells Timothy, Let no one despise your youth. Read First Timothy 4:12.
c2-1ti-0002: Families should care for each other at home. Read First Timothy 5:4 and First Timothy 5:8.
c2-1ti-0003: Paul says we brought nothing into this world and can carry nothing out. Read First Timothy 6:6 and First Timothy 6:7.
c3-1ti-0001: Paul told Timothy to give himself to reading, encouraging, and teaching. Read First Timothy 4:13 and First Timothy 4:15.
c3-1ti-0002: Paul charges Timothy to fight for the faith. Read First Timothy 1:19 and First Timothy 6:12.
c3-1ti-0003: Paul says we trust in the living God, the Savior of all men. Read First Timothy 3:15 and First Timothy 4:10.
c3-1ti-0004: Paul remembers words spoken about Timothy long ago. Read First Timothy 1:18 and First Timothy 4:14.
c1-tit-0001: Paul left Titus behind to set things in order. Read Titus 1:5.
c2-tit-0001: Paul planned to send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus. Read Titus 3:12.
c2-tit-0002: Paul told Titus to show himself a pattern of good works. Read Titus 2:7 and Titus 2:8.
c2-tit-0003: Paul told Titus to avoid foolish disputes. Read Titus 3:9 and Titus 3:10.
c3-tit-0001: Jesus gave Himself for us to set us free. Read Titus 2:13 and Titus 2:14.
c3-tit-0002: The grace and kindness of God our Savior have appeared! Read Titus 2:11, Titus 3:4, and Titus 3:5.
c3-tit-0003: God made a promise before time began. Read Titus 1:2 and Titus 3:7.
c3-tit-0004: Paul calls Titus a true son. Read Titus 1:4 and Titus 2:15.
c1-2pe-0001: The Lord showed Peter something about his future. Read Second Peter 1:14.
c2-2pe-0001: Peter remembers the Father speaking to honor Jesus. Read Second Peter 1:17.
c2-2pe-0002: Peter calls false teachers wells without water. Read Second Peter 2:17 and Second Peter 2:19.
c2-2pe-0003: Scoffers will come in the last days. Read Second Peter 3:3 and Second Peter 3:4.
c3-2pe-0001: Peter says those who do these things will never stumble. Read Second Peter 1:9 and Second Peter 1:10.
c3-2pe-0002: Peter writes to remind his friends. Read Second Peter 1:13 and Second Peter 3:1.
c3-2pe-0003: Peter warns about false teachers who sneak in. Read Second Peter 2:1 and Second Peter 3:17.
c3-2pe-0004: Some teachers use tricky words. Peter tells the truth in Second Peter 1:16 and Second Peter 2:3.
